paragraphs.text: መጽሐፈ፡ ሑረተ፡ ብርሃናት፡ ሰማይ፡ ኵሉ፡ በበ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ዘከመ፡ ኮኑ፡ በበ፡ ሕገጊሆሙ፡ ወበበ፡ ጊዜሆሙ፡ ወበበ፡ ስማቲሆሙ፡ ወበበ፡ ምንቅላቲሆሙ፡ ወበበ፡ አውራኂሆሙ፡ ዘአርአየኒ፡ ዑርኤል፡ መልአኩ፡ ቅዱስ፡ ዘሀሎ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ዘውእቱ፡ መርሖሙ፡ ኵሉ፡ ጽሕፈቶሙ፡ አርአየኒ፡ ዘከመ፡ ኮነ፡ ለኵሉ፡ ዓመታት፡ ዓለም፡ ወእስከ፡ ለዓለም፡ እስከ፡ ይትገበር፡ ፍጥረት፡ ሐዲስ፡ ዘይነብር፡ ለዓለም፡
paragraphs.translit: maṣḥafa ḥurata bərhānāt samāy kwəlu baba ziʾahu zakama konu baba ḥəgagihomu wa-baba gizēhomu wa-baba səmātihomu wa-baba mənqəlātihomu wa-baba ʾawrāḫihomu zaʾarʾayanī ʿUrʾēl malʾaku qəddus zahallo məslēya zawəʾətu marḥomu kwəlu ṣəḥfatomu ʾarʾayanī zakama kona la-kwəlu ʿāmatāt ʿālam wa-ʾəska la-ʿālam ʾəska yətgabbar fəṭrat ḥaddis zayənabbər la-ʿālam

i18n.en: The book of the courses of the luminaries of heaven, each of them as they are, according to their classes, their times, their names, their origins, and their months, which Uriel, the holy angel who was with me, who is their leader, showed me; he showed me their whole record, how it stands for all the years of the world and forever, until the new creation is made which abides forever.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The Astronomical Book opens with two foundational framing-moves.** The opening verse of 1 En 72 establishes (i) Uriel as the principal-revealing-angel of the Astronomical Book — the *malʾaku qəddus* 'holy angel' who is *marḥomu* 'their leader' (over the luminaries); and (ii) the eschatological-horizon of the cosmographic-revelation — the 'new creation that abides forever' (fəṭrat ḥaddis zayənabbər la-ʿālam).

**Uriel as cosmic-administrative-angel.** The Ge'ez *marḥomu* ('their leader') establishes Uriel's portfolio in the Astronomical Book as the cosmic-administrative-angel over the luminaries. The role is consistent with the seven-archangel-list at 1 En 20:2 where Uriel is 'over the world and Tartarus'; the Astronomical Book Uriel is the developed-form of the cosmic-administrative-angel-figure that runs through 1 En 21:5 (Uriel as tour-guide to the place-of-judgement for fallen stars), through ch 75 + 79 + 82 (Uriel's calendrical-leadership), into the 4 Ezra Uriel-as-Ezra's-revelatory-angel tradition, and ultimately into the Hekhalot-Merkavah *Sar ha-Olam* 'Prince of the World' cosmic-administrative-angel-figure. See central entries `uriel-angel-over-luminaries-1-enoch-72-79-82-cross-corpus` and `seven-archangels-list-1-enoch-20-tob-12-rev-8-cross-corpus`.

**The Astronomical Book as a unit.** This verse opens what is — by manuscript-witness — the OLDEST stratum of the 1 Enoch corpus. The Aramaic 4Q208 + 4Q209 fragments (palaeographically dated late 3rd c. BCE per Milik 1976; Tigchelaar-García Martínez DJD XXXVI 2000) predate the Aramaic Book-of-the-Watchers fragments (4Q201/4Q202) and constitute the earliest surviving Enoch material overall. The Astronomical Book has NO Greek witness — the Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus ends mid-ch 32. See central entry `astronomical-book-1-enoch-72-82-aramaic-dss-oldest-witness-unit-entry` and overlay entry `astronomical-book-no-greek-witness-aramaic-geez-only-convention`.

**The 'new creation' eschatological-horizon.** The phrase *fəṭrat ḥaddis* 'new creation' anticipates the eschatological-cosmological renewal that becomes one of the most-persistent Second-Temple-period and downstream eschatological frameworks: Isa 65:17 (*hinnĕnî bôrēʾ šāmayim ḥădāšîm wā-ʾāreṣ ḥădāšâ* 'behold, I create new heavens and a new earth'), Isa 66:22 (the new-heavens-and-new-earth standing-forever), Jub 1:29 + 4:26 (the renewal of all the luminaries), 1 En 91:16 (Apocalypse-of-Weeks), and Rev 21:1 (the new heaven and the new earth). The Astronomical-Book opening positions the cosmographic-revelation as *until the new creation* — that is, the present-cosmic-order (which the Astronomical Book describes) is bracketed within a longer eschatological-horizon. The 'new creation' cluster spans the Second-Temple-Jewish-and-NT eschatological framework as a developed-tradition.

paragraphs.text: ወዝ፡ ሕግ፡ ቀዳማዊ፡ ለብርሃናት፡ ብርሃን፡ ፀሐይ፡ ምንቅላቱ፡ በአናቅጸ፡ ሰማይ፡ ምሥራቃውያን፡ ወዐራቢሁ፡ በአናቅጸ፡ ምዕራባውያን፡ ሰማይ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-zə ḥəg qadāmāwi la-bərhānāt bərhān ḍaḥay mənqəlātu ba-ʾanāqəḍa samāy məśrāqāwəyān wa-ʿarābihu ba-ʾanāqəḍa məʿrābāwəyān samāy

i18n.en: And this is the first law of the luminaries: the light of the sun has its rising in the eastern gates of heaven, and its setting in the western gates of heaven.

paragraphs.text: ወርእኩ፡ ስድስቱ፡ አናቅጸ፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወስድስቱ፡ አናቅጸ፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይዐርብ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወወርኅሂ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በውስቴቶሙ፡ ወመራኅያነ፡ ከዋክብት፡ ምስለ፡ መሪሖሙ፡ ስድስቱ፡ በምሥራቅ፡ ወስድስቱ፡ በምዕራብ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ በበ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ተራሕው፡ ድኅረ፡ ካልኡ፡ ወብዙኃንኒ፡ ጠባት፡ በኀበ፡ ካልኦቶሙ፡ በኤምነ፡ ወበፅግመ፡ እማንቱ፡ አናቅጽ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-rəʾku sədəstu ʾanāqəḍa ʾəmənnehomu yəwaḍḍəʾ ḍaḥay wa-sədəstu ʾanāqəḍa ʾəmənnehomu yəʿarrəb ḍaḥay wa-warḫəni yəwaḍḍəʾ wa-yəʿarrəb ba-wəstētomu wa-marāḫəyāna kawākəbt məsla marihomu sədəstu ba-məśrāq wa-sədəstu ba-məʿrāb kwəlomu baba ziʾahu tarāḥwə dəḫra kāləʾu wa-bəzuḫāni ṭabāt ba-ḫaba kāləʾotomu ba-ʾēmna wa-ba-ḍəgma ʾəmāntu ʾanāqəḍ

i18n.en: And I saw six gates through which the sun comes forth, and six gates through which the sun sets; and the moon also rises and sets in those gates, together with the leaders of the stars and those whom they lead: six in the east and six in the west, all of them ranged one after another in their order; and many side-windows are alongside them on the right and on the left of those gates.

paragraphs.text: ወቀዲሙ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ብርሃኑ፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ዘውእቱ፡ ስሙ፡ በአንቀጽ፡ ራብዕ፡ እምነ፡ ስድስቱ፡ አናቅጽ፡ እማንቱ፡ ቀዳማዊያን፡ ምሥራቃውያን፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-qadimu yəwaḍḍəʾ bərhānu la-ḍaḥay ʿabəy zawəʾətu səmu ba-ʾanqaḍ rābəʿ ʾəmənna sədəstu ʾanāqəḍ ʾəmāntu qadāmāwəyān məśrāqāwəyān

i18n.en: And first there comes forth the great luminary, whose name is the sun, by the fourth of those six eastern gates.

paragraphs.text: ወውስተ፡ ይእቲ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ራብዕት፡ እንተ፡ እምኔሃ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ቀዳማዌ፡ ወርኀ፡ ሀለዉ፡ ዐሠርቱ፡ ወክልኤቱ፡ መሣክው፡ ክሥቱት፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ነበልባል፡ ሶበ፡ ይትረኀዉ፡ በበ፡ ጊዜሆሙ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-wəsta yəʾəti ʾanqaḍ rābəʿt ʾənta ʾəmənnehā yəwaḍḍəʾ ḍaḥay qadāmāwē warḫa hallawu ʿaśartu wa-kəlʾētu masākəw kəśtut ʾəmənnehomu yəwaḍḍəʾ nabalbāl soba yətrəḫḫawu baba gizēhomu

i18n.en: And in that fourth gate from which the sun comes forth in the first month there are twelve windows opened, from which a flame issues whenever they are opened in their seasons.

paragraphs.text: ወሶበ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ በሰማይ፡ ይወፅእ፡ በይእቲ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ራብዕት፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በከመ፡ ሕገጊሁ፡ በውስተ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ራብዒት፡ እንተ፡ ምዕራብ፡ ሰማይ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-soba yəwaḍḍəʾ ḍaḥay ba-samāy yəwaḍḍəʾ ba-yəʾəti ʾanqaḍ rābəʿt śallāsā mawāʿəla wa-yəʿarrəb bakama ḥəgagihu ba-wəsta ʾanqaḍ rābəʿit ʾənta məʿrāb samāy

i18n.en: When the sun rises in heaven, it comes forth through that fourth gate for thirty days, and sets, according to its law, in the fourth gate of the western heaven.

paragraphs.text: ወበእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ይነውኅ፡ መዓልት፡ እምነ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይትዌሰክ፡ መዓልት፡ እምነ፡ ሌሊት፡ ዘእንበለ፡ ይብጻሕ፡ ብርሃኑ፡ ለፀሐይ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ራብዕተ፡ ይነዊኅ፡ መዓልት፡ ቅሩበ፡ ካዕበ፡ ምስለ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ መዓልት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ ይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-ba-ʾəmāntu mawāʿəl yənawwəḫ maʿālt ʾəmənna lēlit wa-yətwēsak maʿālt ʾəmənna lēlit za-ʾənbala yəbṣāḥ bərhānu la-ḍaḥay ʾanqaḍa rābəʿta yənawiḫ maʿālt qəruba kāʿba məsla lēlit wa-yəkawwən maʿālt ʿaśarta kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-lēlit yəkawwən ʿaśarta kəfālāta

i18n.en: And in those days the day grows longer than the night, and the day continues to grow longer than the night until the sun's rising reaches the fourth gate. The day approaches twice the night, and the day amounts to twelve parts and the night to ten parts.

paragraphs.commentary: **The 22-part day-ratio system begins here.** The ratio 12+10 = 22 parts inaugurates one of two parallel day-ratio systems that coexist within 1 En 72 without explicit harmonization. The other system — the 18-part system at the solstice-extremes — appears at vv. 11 + 21 (12+6 = 18 parts). The dual-system situation is one of the most-discussed astronomical-textual-cruxes of the Astronomical Book; the WoH translation preserves both systems verbatim without harmonization, per the source-internal-inconsistency convention. See overlay entry `18-vs-22-part-day-ratio-scholarly-crux-1-enoch-72-7-no-harmonization-convention` and the foundational scholarly treatment in O. Neugebauer *The Astronomical Chapters of the Ethiopic Book of Enoch (72-82)* (1981; reprinted as appendix to Black 1985).

paragraphs.text: ወይወፅእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምይእቲ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ራብዕት፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በራብዒት፡ ወይትገብእ፡ ኀበ፡ ኃምስት፡ አንቀጽ፡ በምሥራቅ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ እምኔሃ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በኃምስት፡ አንቀጽ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmyəʾəti ʾanqaḍ rābəʿt wa-yəʿarrəb ba-rābəʿit wa-yətgabbəʾ ḫaba ḫāməst ʾanqaḍ ba-məśrāq śallāsā mawāʿəla wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ ʾəmənnehā wa-yəʿarrəb ba-ḫāməst ʾanqaḍ

i18n.en: And the sun comes forth from that fourth gate and sets in the fourth gate, and it returns to the fifth gate in the east for thirty days, and it comes forth from it and sets in the fifth gate.

paragraphs.text: ወአመ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ኃምስት፡ አንቀጽ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ይነውኅ፡ መዓልት፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ሠለስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ ዘጠዐ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-ʾama yəwaḍḍəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna ḫāməst ʾanqaḍ śallāsā mawāʿəla yənawwəḫ maʿālt wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta śallasta kəfālāta wa-lēlit zaṭaʿ kəfālāta

i18n.en: And when the sun comes forth from the fifth gate for thirty days, the day grows longer, and amounts to thirteen parts, and the night to nine parts.

paragraphs.text: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ምሥራቀ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ውስተ፡ ሳድስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በሳድስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ሠላሳ፡ ወአሐደ፡ መዋዕለ፡ በእንተ፡ ምልክቱ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay məśrāqa wa-yəbawwəʾ wəsta sādəs ʾanqaḍ wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ wa-yəʿarrəb ba-sādəs ʾanqaḍ śallāsā wa-ʾaḥada mawāʿəla ba-ʾənta məlkətu

i18n.en: And the sun returns to the east and enters the sixth gate, and it comes forth and sets in the sixth gate for thirty-one days, on account of its sign.

paragraphs.text: ወይነውኅ፡ መዓልት፡ እምነ፡ ይእቲ፡ ሳድስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ካዕበ፡ ምስለ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ መዓልት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ስድስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ maʿālt ʾəmənna yəʾəti sādəs ʾanqaḍ kāʿba məsla lēlit wa-yəkawwən maʿālt ʿaśarta wa-kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-lēlit yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən sədəsta kəfālāta

i18n.en: And on that day the day becomes twice as long as the night, and the day amounts to twelve parts, and the night is shortened and amounts to six parts.

paragraphs.text: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ውስተ፡ ኃምስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በኃምስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay wa-yəbawwəʾ wəsta ḫāməs ʾanqaḍ wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ wa-yəʿarrəb ba-ḫāməs ʾanqaḍ śallāsā mawāʿəla

i18n.en: And the sun returns and enters the fifth gate, and it comes forth and sets in the fifth gate for thirty days.

paragraphs.text: ወይነውኅ፡ መዓልት፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ሠለስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ ዘጠዐ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ maʿālt wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta śallasta kəfālāta wa-lēlit zaṭaʿ kəfālāta

i18n.en: And the day amounts to thirteen parts and the night to nine parts.

paragraphs.text: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ኃምስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ራብዐ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በራብዕ፡ አንቀጽ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna ḫāməs ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ rābəʿa ʾanqaḍa śallāsā mawāʿəla yəwaḍḍəʾ wa-yəʿarrəb ba-rābəʿ ʾanqaḍ

i18n.en: And the sun returns from the fifth gate and enters the fourth gate for thirty days; it comes forth and sets in the fourth gate.

paragraphs.text: ወይትዐረዩ፡ መዓልት፡ ምስለ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይትከበቡ፡ ወይከውን፡ መዓልት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወአሐደ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ ይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወአሐደ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətʿarrayu maʿālt məsla lēlit wa-yətkababu wa-yəkawwən maʿālt ʿaśarta wa-ʾaḥada kəfālāta wa-lēlit yəkawwən ʿaśarta wa-ʾaḥada kəfālāta

i18n.en: And the day becomes equal to the night, and they encompass one another; the day amounts to eleven parts and the night to eleven parts.

paragraphs.text: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ውስተ፡ ሣልስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በሣልስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ሠላሳ፡ ወአሐደ፡ መዋዕለ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay wa-yəbawwəʾ wəsta śāləs ʾanqaḍ wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ wa-yəʿarrəb ba-śāləs ʾanqaḍ śallāsā wa-ʾaḥada mawāʿəla

i18n.en: And the sun returns and enters the third gate, and it comes forth and sets in the third gate for thirty-one days.

paragraphs.text: ወይነውኅ፡ ሌሊት፡ እምነ፡ መዓልት፡ እስከ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ሣልስ፡ ወይከውን፡ ሌሊት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ ይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ lēlit ʾəmənna maʿālt ʾəska ʾanqaḍ śāləs wa-yəkawwən lēlit ʿaśarta kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-maʿālt yəkawwən ʿaśarta kəfālāta

i18n.en: And the night grows longer than the day, until the third gate; the night amounts to twelve parts and the day to ten parts.

paragraphs.text: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ሣልስ፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ካልዕተ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ምሥራቅ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna śāləs ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ kāləʿta ʾanqaḍa məśrāq śallāsā mawāʿəla

i18n.en: And the sun returns from the third gate and enters the second gate in the east for thirty days.

paragraphs.text: ወይነውኅ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ሠለስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ዘጠዐ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ lēlit wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta śallasta kəfālāta wa-maʿālt yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən zaṭaʿ kəfālāta

i18n.en: And the night grows longer and amounts to thirteen parts, and the day is shortened and amounts to nine parts.

paragraphs.text: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ካልዕት፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ቀዳሚተ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሠላሳ፡ ወአሐደ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በቀዳሚት፡ አንቀጽ፡ እንተ፡ ምዕራብ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna kāləʿt ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ qadāmita ʾanqaḍa śallāsā wa-ʾaḥada mawāʿəla wa-yəʿarrəb ba-qadāmit ʾanqaḍ ʾənta məʿrāb

i18n.en: And the sun returns from the second gate and enters the first gate for thirty-one days, and sets in the first gate of the west.

paragraphs.text: ወይነውኅ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ ካዕበ፡ ምስለ፡ መዓልት፡ ወሌሊት፡ ይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ ስድስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ lēlit wa-yəkawwən kāʿba məsla maʿālt wa-lēlit yəkawwən ʿaśarta kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-maʿālt sədəsta kəfālāta

i18n.en: And the night grows longer and becomes twice as long as the day: the night amounts to twelve parts and the day to six parts.

paragraphs.text: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ቀዳሚት፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ካልዕተ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna qadāmit ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ kāləʿta ʾanqaḍa śallāsā mawāʿəla

i18n.en: And the sun returns from the first gate and enters the second gate for thirty days.

paragraphs.text: ወይነውኅ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ሠለስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ዘጠዐ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ lēlit wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta śallasta kəfālāta wa-maʿālt yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən zaṭaʿ kəfālāta

i18n.en: And the night amounts to thirteen parts, and the day is shortened and amounts to nine parts.

paragraphs.text: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ካልዕት፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ሣልስተ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በሣልስት፡ አንቀጽ፡ እንተ፡ ምዕራብ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna kāləʿt ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ śāləsta ʾanqaḍa śallāsā mawāʿəla wa-yəʿarrəb ba-śāləst ʾanqaḍ ʾənta məʿrāb

i18n.en: And the sun returns from the second gate and enters the third gate for thirty days, and sets in the third gate of the west.

paragraphs.text: ወበይእቲ፡ ጊዜ፡ ይትዐረዩ፡ መዓልት፡ ምስለ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ ሌሊት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወአሐደ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ ይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወአሐደ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-ba-yəʾəti gizē yətʿarrayu maʿālt məsla lēlit wa-yəkawwən lēlit ʿaśarta wa-ʾaḥada kəfālāta wa-maʿālt yəkawwən ʿaśarta wa-ʾaḥada kəfālāta

i18n.en: And at that time the day becomes equal to the night: the night amounts to eleven parts and the day to eleven parts.

paragraphs.text: ወይትገብእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ እምነ፡ ሣልስት፡ አንቀጽ፡ ወይበውእ፡ ራብዕተ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሠላሳ፡ ወአሐደ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ እምኔሃ፡ ወይዐርብ፡ በራብዕ፡ አንቀጽ፡ እንተ፡ ምዕራብ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾ ḍaḥay ʾəmənna śāləst ʾanqaḍ wa-yəbawwəʾ rābəʿta ʾanqaḍa śallāsā wa-ʾaḥada mawāʿəla wa-yəwaḍḍəʾ ʾəmənnehā wa-yəʿarrəb ba-rābəʿ ʾanqaḍ ʾənta məʿrāb

i18n.en: And the sun returns from the third gate and enters the fourth gate for thirty-one days, and comes forth from it and sets in the fourth gate of the west.

paragraphs.text: ወይነውኅ፡ መዓልት፡ ካዕበ፡ ምስለ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይከውን፡ መዓልት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yənawwəḫ maʿālt kāʿba məsla lēlit wa-yəkawwən maʿālt ʿaśarta kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-lēlit yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta kəfālāta

i18n.en: And the day grows longer than the night: the day amounts to twelve parts and the night is shortened and amounts to ten parts.

paragraphs.text: ወዝ፡ ሕግ፡ ወሑረት፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ወግብአቱ፡ ስብዐ፡ እምነ፡ ሙያኖሙ፡ ግብአቱ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-zə ḥəg wa-ḥurat la-ḍaḥay wa-gəbʾatu səbʿa ʾəmənna muyānomu gəbʾatu

i18n.en: This is the law and the course of the sun, and its return — sevenfold it returns from its turnings.

paragraphs.text: ወይትዌሰክ፡ ይእቲ፡ ሙያው፡ ለመዓልት፡ ካዕበ፡ ወትትኄፀጽ፡ ለሌሊት፡ በስድስቱ፡ መንገላት፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətwēsak yəʾəti muyāw la-maʿālt kāʿba wa-tətḫēḍaḍ la-lēlit ba-sədəstu mangalāt

i18n.en: And that turning is added to the day, and the night is shortened, through the six paths.

paragraphs.text: ወትበጽሕ፡ ሙያው፡ ሰማይ፡ መዓልት፡ መዓልት፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወሌሊት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ስድስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-təbaṣṣəḥ muyāw samāy maʿālt maʿālt ʿaśarta wa-kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-lēlit yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən sədəsta kəfālāta

i18n.en: And the turning of heaven reaches its extreme: the day amounts to twelve parts and the night is shortened and amounts to six parts.

paragraphs.text: ወይትኄፀጽ፡ መዓልት፡ እምነ፡ ሌሊት፡ ወይትገብእ፡ ሌሊት፡ እስከ፡ መንገል፡ ስድስት፡ ወይከውን፡ ዐሠርተ፡ ወክልኤተ፡ ክፋላተ፡ ወመዓልት፡ የሐጽጽ፡ ወይከውን፡ ስድስተ፡ ክፋላተ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yətḫēḍaḍ maʿālt ʾəmənna lēlit wa-yətgabbəʾ lēlit ʾəska mangal sədəst wa-yəkawwən ʿaśarta wa-kəlʾēta kəfālāta wa-maʿālt yaḥaḍḍəḍ wa-yəkawwən sədəsta kəfālāta

i18n.en: And the day is shortened, and the night returns, until the sixth path: the night amounts to twelve parts and the day is shortened and amounts to six parts.

paragraphs.text: ወእምዘ፡ ይትዌሰክ፡ መዓልት፡ ለመዓልት፡ ወይትዌሰክ፡ ሌሊት፡ ለሌሊት፡ ወይፈጽም፡ ኆለቆሙ፡ በበ፡ ጊዜሁ፡ ሠለስቱ፡ ምእት፡ ስድሳ፡ ወአርባዕቱ፡ መዋዕል፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-ʾəmza yətwēsak maʿālt la-maʿālt wa-yətwēsak lēlit la-lēlit wa-yəfaṣṣəm ḫolaqomu baba gizēhu śallastu məʾət sədsā wa-ʾarbāʿtu mawāʿəl

i18n.en: And from then the day adds to the day, and the night adds to the night; and they complete their count in their seasons — three hundred and sixty-four days.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The 364-day-year statement — the calendrical-identity-keystone of the Astronomical Book and the broader Qumran-Enochic-Jubilees corpus.** This verse is the explicit-foundational-statement of the 364-day solar calendar: the sun's annual circuit through the twelve gates of heaven completes 364 days. The mathematical-elegance of the 364-day year (52 weeks × 7 days = 364 days; four seasons × 91 days each = 364 days; festival-dates always fall on the same day of the week) is essential to the calendar's appeal and its identity-marker status. The 364-day calendar is the calendrical-identity-keystone of the Qumran community vis-à-vis the proto-Rabbinic / Pharisaic Temple-Establishment lunar-solar tradition.

**Cross-corpus to Jubilees 6:32-38.** The Jubilees parallel polemic at 6:32-38 makes the calendrical-identity-keystone status explicit: 'they will forget the new moons and the times and the sabbaths, and they will make mistakes in all the new months and times and sabbaths ... if they walk in the times of the Gentiles and follow their ways'. The 364-day calendar is presented in Jubilees as the divinely-ordained calendar inscribed in the heavenly-tablets; the proto-Rabbinic lunar calendar is presented as cosmic-disorder and ritual-impurity.

**Cross-corpus to the Qumran calendrical texts.** The Qumran community produced an extensive corpus of calendrical-implementation-texts (4Q319 Otot; 4Q320-4Q321a + 4Q325-4Q330 Mishmarot; 4Q252; 4QMMT B; 11Q5 col 27 'David's Compositions' attributing 364 psalms-per-year to David; CD 16:2-3). The 364-day calendar was a working-calendar of the Qumran community, not merely a theoretical-ideal.

**The 364-day-vs-365.25-day mathematical problem.** The 364-day year is short of the actual tropical year (~365.25 days) by 1.25 days per year; over time, this discrepancy accumulates. Multiple harmonization-strategies have been proposed in scholarship (Glessmer 1999; Beckwith 1996; Stern 2001); the WoH translation preserves the source-text 364-day-year without modernization. See central entry `qumran-364-day-solar-calendar-polemic-1-enoch-72-82-jubilees-cross-corpus` and overlay entry `364-day-solar-calendar-rendering-convention`.

paragraphs.text: ወይእቲ፡ ናኦተ፡ ሙያው፡ ሙያው፡ ስሉሰ፡ ምእት፡ ስድሳ፡ ወአርባዕቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ዘውእቱ፡ ኆለቅ፡ ለዓመት፡ ዘሐቅ፡ ናኦተ፡ ምሉእ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yəʾəti nāʾota muyāw muyāw sǝlusa məʾət sədsā wa-ʾarbāʿtu mawāʿəl zawəʾətu ḫolaq la-ʿāmat zaḥaqq nāʾota məluʾ

i18n.en: And this is the measure of the turning of the turnings: three hundred and sixty-four days — this is the count of the true full year.

paragraphs.text: ናኦተ፡ ሙያው፡ ለመዓልት፡ ወለሌሊት፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ወንዕሰት፡ ሙያው፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ዘይትዌሰክ፡ ብርሃኑ፡ ወዘይትኄፀጽ፡ ብርሃኑ፡
paragraphs.translit: nāʾota muyāw la-maʿālt wa-la-lēlit la-ḍaḥay wa-nəʿsat muyāw la-ḍaḥay zayətwēsak bərhānu wa-zayətḫēḍaḍ bərhānu

i18n.en: Such is the measure of the turning of day and night for the sun; and such is the lesser turning of the sun whose light grows and whose light is diminished.

paragraphs.text: ወዝ፡ ሕግ፡ ወሑረት፡ ለብርሃኑ፡ ለዐቢይ፡ ብርሃን፡ ዘፀሐይ፡ ዘርእኩ፡ ወዘስሙ፡ በበ፡ ሕገጊሁ፡ ኮነ፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-zə ḥəg wa-ḥurat la-bərhānu la-ʿabəy bərhān za-ḍaḥay zarəʾku wa-zasəmu baba ḥəgagihu kona

i18n.en: And this is the law and the course of the light of the great luminary, the sun, which I saw, and whose name is according to its laws.

paragraphs.text: ወብርሃኑ፡ ይትዌሰክ፡ ወይትኄፀጽ፡ በበ፡ ጊዜሁ፡ ኵሉ፡ በበ፡ ሕገጊሁ፡ ወሰዓታቲሁ፡ ኵሉ፡ ይትከውን፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-bərhānu yətwēsak wa-yətḫēḍaḍ baba gizēhu kwəlu baba ḥəgagihu wa-saʿātātihu kwəlu yətkawwan

i18n.en: And its light waxes and wanes each in its season, all according to its laws and its hours; all things come to be.

paragraphs.text: ወይእቲ፡ ይእቲ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ዐባይ፡ እንተ፡ ሰብዐ፡ ብርሃና፡ ድልዋ፡ ለወርኅ፡ ብርሃና፡ በዐቢይ፡ ኆለቅ፡ ዘብርሃኑ፡ ይትዐረዩ፡ ሰብዐ፡ ምስለ፡ ብርሃና፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ወይትዌቅሕ፡ ብርሃና፡ ለወርኅ፡ ወሰብዐ፡ ምስለ፡ ብርሃና፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ይትፈቀድ፡ ወይከውን፡ ምሉአ፡ ብርሃና፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ወሰብዐ፡ ምስለ፡ ብርሃና፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ይትፈቀድ፡ ብርሃና፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-yəʾəti yəʾəti ḍaḥay ʿabay ʾənta sabʿa bərhānā dəlwā la-warḫ bərhānā ba-ʿabəy ḫolaq zabərhānu yətʿarrayu sabʿa məsla bərhānā la-ḍaḥay wa-yətwaḳḳəḥ bərhānā la-warḫ wa-sabʿa məsla bərhānā la-ḍaḥay yətfaqqad wa-yəkawwən məluʾa bərhānā la-ḍaḥay wa-sabʿa məsla bərhānā la-ḍaḥay yətfaqqad bərhānā

i18n.en: And this is the great sun whose light is sevenfold the moon's; in the great reckoning, its light measured sevenfold against the moon's light, and the moon's light is diminished. Sevenfold against the sun's light is reckoned, and the sun's light becomes full; and sevenfold against the sun's light her light is reckoned.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The 7:1 sun:moon luminosity ratio + the corrupted-Ge'ez scribal-repetition.** The verse states the 7:1 sun:moon luminosity ratio that organizes the Astronomical Book's framework of the 'greater luminary' (sun) and 'lesser luminary' (moon) — paralleling the Gen 1:14-19 *meʾōrôt gĕdōlîm / qāṭān* framework. The 7:1 ratio is one of the schematic-ideal-ratios characteristic of the Astronomical Book; it does not correspond to modern-astronomical measurements of solar-vs-lunar luminosity but operates within the source-text-schematic register.

**The Ge'ez of v. 37 is textually difficult.** The repeated phrasing 'sevenfold against the sun's light is reckoned' appears multiple times in the Ge'ez witness — Charles 1912 noted the scribal-repetition as corrupted; Knibb 1978 preserves the Ge'ez verbatim; the modern critical-editions (Nickelsburg-VanderKam 2012 Hermeneia vol 2) document the corruption without proposing definitive emendation. The WoH translation preserves the Ge'ez verbatim per the per-verse layered-witness convention.

**Cross-corpus to Isa 30:26 — the eschatological sun-moon-light-reversal.** Isa 30:26 *wĕ-hāyâ ʾôr ha-lĕbānâ kĕ-ʾôr ha-ḥammâ wĕ-ʾôr ha-ḥammâ yihyeh šiḇʿātayim* 'and the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold' — the eschatological-reversal of the natural-cosmic-order where the moon's light becomes equal to the sun's and the sun's light becomes sevenfold its present-state. The Isa 30:26 framework parallels the 1 En 72:37 7:1 ratio but inverts the present-state-ratio into the eschatological-reversal.
